notes: §1985:VI.6.24.3 SR3: "If literal-1 is numeric, then it must be an unsigned integer." ControlFlowBinder.ScreenStopLiteral (85 only, where STOP literal exists) reports COBOL6817 unless Cobol85OperandForms.IsUnsignedIntegerLiteral holds: no PLUS or MINUS and a lone INTEGERLIT token; the witness is STOP 1.5. Probes (work-rd-09/stop): b) refused COBOL6817: ALL "A", ALL 'XY', ALL ZERO, ALL SPACES, ALL QUOTES, ALL symbolic-character, 1.5, 1.0, .5, -1, +1; accepted and run: ZERO, SPACE, QUOTE, HIGH-VALUE, "HELLO", 0, the 18-digit 123456789012345678 (each printed, then 'AFTER'); c) X"41" is COBOL0900 at 85, and the whole STOP literal statement is COBOL0902 at --std 2002. f) 0 and 18 digits are accepted; a negative or explicitly signed value and any literal with a digit right of the point are refused; a nonnumeric literal is outside the rule and accepted.

next.reason: In 1985 literal-1 is the operand of the STOP literal-1 form, the pause that is an alternative to RUN: 'the execution of the run unit is suspended and literal-1 is communicated to the operator' (§1985:VI.6.24.4 GR4). 1985 marks that form obsolete. 2023 has no such form, since §2023:14.9.42.2 always requires RUN. Its literal-1 is a new 'WITH ERROR/NORMAL STATUS' operand passed to the operating system. §2023:14.9.42.3 SR3 ('If literal-1 is numeric, it shall be an integer') shares only the operand name, and the 1985 requirement went with the pause form.
